messages:
anna-support: Customer reports brief spikes of 429s during bursts (10s window). They say quotas look fine in the console but latency + error spikes correlate with a flurry of short requests. Can someone help triage?

maria-cs: Pasted the customer's repro they just sent: they run many small completions in parallel (avg prompt 120 tokens) with continuous batching on. Using Dedicated pool, model=redwood-alpha-7b. Example curl:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-7b","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":50}'
```

Response during spike: 429 with headers: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RW-Quota-Burst: 30
```

They say the X-RW-Quota-Burst looks weird (small) and they don't see sustained usage to justify 0 remaining.

sam-eng: Thanks — a few quick hypothesis: continuous batching + KV cache warmup can look like throttle during sudden bursts of small prompts. If many new prefixes hit the KV cache, first requests stall on cache fill and we can see backpressure that manifests as 429s from the token bucket. Also check per-route token bucket (route-level throttle) vs account quota.

lee-ml: Agree. Two sub-issues to check: 1) prefix-starvation / cache cold starts — lots of unique prefixes cause the runtime to prefetch KV which increases in-flight tokens; 2) batch sizing / max_wait_ms — if max_wait_ms is high, short requests may get queued causing perceived latency and then a sudden flush that trips burst limits.

sam-eng: Can you ask customer to ship us a short repro script that includes timing? Also ask them to capture response headers for both 200 and 429s. Meanwhile I want to look at their Dedicated pool metrics for: inflight batches, batch size distribution, kv-cache miss rate, and per-route token bucket token counts.

maria-cs: They provided timings: a concurrent flood of ~120 requests over 8s. Most prompts unique. Pool size: 4xA10G. Observed baseline RPS small (~5rps) but burst to ~15rps for ~10s. They attached console screenshots (not in thread) showing burst quota consumption spike.

sam-eng: Quick diagnostic steps we can run (ask customer):
- Re-run with a simple single-threaded loop to reproduce, capture headers.
- Try setting header `X-RW-Debug: kv` to get kv cache debug (we can enable for them).
- Temporarily set client-side max_concurrency to 8 to smooth bursts.

lee-ml: Config suggestions to reduce perceived throttling:
```yaml
runtime:
  continuous_batching:
    max_wait_ms: 5      # reduce queuing delay
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
  kv_cache:
    prefetch: true      # warm KV on known prefixes
    prefetch_workers: 4
```

Note: prefetch increases background traffic but reduces cold miss stalls.

maria-cs: Customer asked whether lowering max_wait_ms might increase token usage and cause more 429s — they are worried tuning could worsen bursting.

sam-eng: Good question. There is a tradeoff: lower max_wait_ms reduces per-request latency by limiting queuing, but it may reduce batching efficiency (more small batches) which can increase per-token cost and potentially higher request counts. However in their case many prompts are unique so batching benefit is limited; the primary win is reducing head-of-line blocking that leads to many simultaneous cache fills. Prefetch helps here.

lee-ml: Also check their route-level burst allowance. The header `X-RW-Quota-Burst` comes from our burst controller. For Dedicated pools the default per-route burst is conservative. If this customer needs predictable short bursts we can temporarily bump their route burst cap (policy change) and monitor.

sam-eng: I've provisionally opened a low-risk tweak: enable kv prefetch for their pool and bump route burst from 30 -> 90 for 24h while we observe. maria, can you get customer approval? I'll also attach a short script they can run that toggles prefetch header for testing:

```bash
# test script: toggle prefetch header to compare
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -H "X-RW-Prefetch: 1" \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-7b","prompt":"test $i","max_tokens":20}' &
  sleep 0.05
done
wait
```

maria-cs: Customer approved temporary bump and agreed to run test script tonight UTC. They also asked we keep them posted on any config changes.

deploy-bot: Created ticket INC-2026-345 and applied ephemeral policy: route-burst=90 (expires 24h).

anna-support: Thanks team — plan: (1) monitor Dedicated pool metrics and kv miss rate over the next 24h, (2) collect customer test run with X-RW-Prefetch header on/off, (3) if prefetch improves 429s, propose permanent prefetch + adjust burst cap. I'll update customer and close thread after 24h observation. :thumbsup:

maria-cs: I'll coordinate the customer test and paste results here when ready.

sam-eng: If we still see 429s after prefetch + bump, next steps: enable detailed rate-limiter debug (will show token bucket drain events) and consider staged increase of pool capacity or a short circuit to an alternate model variant during bursts.

anna-support: Copy. Closing triage for now — will reopen if new 429s after tests.
